label: Adding noise until only noise is left
context: A 2D dataset of about 400 points lying on two interleaved crescents ('two moons') is the data distribution p_0. Phase 1 (forward process): every point moves as x_sigma = x_0 + sigma * eps with a fixed per-point Gaussian eps; sigma grows from 0 to about 4 times the data spread on a log scale; show a small sigma slider/gauge on the right edge labelled 'σ' with its current value. The crescents blur, then become one round Gaussian blob. Phase 2: freeze at high sigma and caption 'only noise is left: p_σ ≈ N(0, σ² I)'. Phase 3 (reverse): run the exact reverse path back to sigma = 0 (just the same interpolation backwards), with points coloured by which crescent they came from (blue #0B4FC0 and warm #B4552F) appearing as colour only once sigma is small. Caption the reverse phase 'a denoiser has to learn to walk this back'. Canvas is responsive: width anywhere from 340 to 900 px, height 400 px; derive every size and position from width and height, keep all text at least 11 px and fully inside the canvas, and on narrow widths stack or shrink rather than overlap. Loop forever on a cycle of 10 to 16 s with smooth easing between phases. White background. Put a one-line phase caption at the top centre that changes with the phase. No title inside the canvas (the card has one). Use plain sans-serif labels.

spec.title: Adding noise until only noise is left
spec.caption: Each point of the two-moons data p₀ is pushed along x_σ = x₀ + σ·ε with a fixed ε, until p_σ ≈ N(0, σ² I). The reverse is the same path run backwards, which is the path a denoiser must learn to follow.
